root_cause.text: The Octeontx2 AF driver dereferenced the shared firmware data pointer `rvu->fwdata` in CGX/RPM- and SDP-related paths without validating that firmware data was mapped, which is invalid on boards booted without a MAC block.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit NULL checks before accessing `rvu->fwdata` in `rvu_sdp_init()` (`if (rvu->fwdata && rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid)`) and `rvu_mbox_handler_cgx_set_link_mode()` (`if (!rvu->fwdata) return LMAC_AF_ERR_FIRMWARE_DATA_NOT_MAPPED;`), while the CVE/commit message states that “Accessing fwdata, on boards booted with out MAC block” caused kernel panics.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds explicit NULL checks before accessing `rvu->fwdata` in `rvu_sdp_init()` (`if (rvu->fwdata && rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid)`) and `rvu_mbox_handler_cgx_set_link_mode()` (`if (!rvu->fwdata) return LMAC_AF_ERR_FIRMWARE_DATA_NOT_MAPPED;`), while the CVE/commit message states that “Accessing fwdata, on boards booted with out MAC block” caused kernel panics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early firmware-data presence check in cgx link mode handling to return a specific error when fwdata is not mapped.
intent_record.what: A new null check was added at the start of rvu_mbox_handler_cgx_set_link_mode() to test whether rvu->fwdata is unset, and the function now immediately returns LMAC_AF_ERR_FIRMWARE_DATA_NOT_MAPPED when that condition is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now fails early when firmware data has not been mapped, preventing later code from operating without required firmware state and avoiding invalid access or incorrect link mode handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null check for `rvu->fwdata` in `rvu_sdp_init()` to avoid crashing when firmware channel data is unavailable.
intent_record.what: The condition `if (rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid)` was changed to `if (rvu->fwdata && rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid)` in `rvu_sdp_init()`, adding a null check for `rvu->fwdata` before accessing its `channel_data` field.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents dereferencing a null `rvu->fwdata` pointer when firmware data is absent, so the SDP initialization block is skipped instead of causing a crash.

grouping_result.intent: Add an early firmware-data presence check in cgx link mode handling to return a specific error when fwdata is not mapped.
Add a null check for `rvu->fwdata` in `rvu_sdp_init()` to avoid crashing when firmware channel data is unavailable.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds a guard before CGX link mode code uses rvu->fwdata, preventing dereference when firmware data is not mapped, which matches the stated root cause.
The change directly addresses the root cause by validating `rvu->fwdata` before it is dereferenced in an SDP-related path, preventing crashes when firmware data is not mapped.

candidates.rationale: This directly dereferences rvu->fwdata without checking whether firmware data is mapped, matching the root cause and causing a crash on boards without a MAC block.
This also dereferences rvu->fwdata without validation; if fwdata is NULL, taking the address of channel_data.info triggers the same invalid access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences `rvu->fwdata` to access `channel_data.valid` without first validating that `rvu->fwdata` is non-NULL, which matches the root cause on systems where firmware data is not mapped.
This statement also dereferences `rvu->fwdata` without a NULL check by taking the address of a field within it, leading to invalid access when firmware data is absent.

Author: Hariprasad Kelam <hkelam@marvell.com>
Date:   Mon Feb 12 18:45:23 2024 +0530

    Octeontx2-af: Fetch MAC channel info from firmware
    
    Packet ingress and egress MAC/serdes channel numbers are configurable
    on CN10K series of silicons. These channel numbers inturn used while
    installing MCAM rules to match ingress/egress port. Fetch these channel
    numbers from firmware at driver init time.
    
    Signed-off-by: Hariprasad K
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it directly shows the newly added firmware-data access in the relevant SDP init path. The vulnerable construct is present: `if (rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid) { ... pfvf->sdp_info = &rvu->fwdata->channel_data.info; ... }`. This dereferences `rvu->fwdata` twice (`rvu->fwdata->channel_data.valid` and `rvu->fwdata->channel_data.info`) with no prior NULL check on `rvu->fwdata`. The root cause states that AF code was vulnerable when shared firmware data was not mapped on boards booted without a MAC block. This function contains exactly that unchecked dereference pattern. The fix is not present here because correct handling would require validating that `rvu->fwdata` is mapped/non-NULL before accessing `channel_data`, but no such guard appears in the shown code.

    dual SDP blocks supported in 98xx silicon.
    
    Signed-off-by: Radha Mohan Chintakuntla <radhac@marvell
bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function bodies in this new file are sufficient to determine whether the specific root-cause construct is present. The stated vulnerability is dereferencing `rvu->fwdata` without validating that firmware data was mapped. In this snippet, none of the functions access `rvu->fwdata` at all. For example, `rvu_sdp_init(struct rvu *rvu)` uses `rvu->pf[...]` and `rvu->dev`; `rvu_mbox_handler_set_sdp_chan_info(...)` uses `rvu_get_pfvf(rvu, ...)` and `pfvf->sdp_info`; `rvu_mbox_handler_get_sdp_chan_info(...)` uses `rvu->hw`, `rvu_get_blkaddr(...)`, and `rvu_read64(...)`. Since the vulnerable construct—an unchecked dereference of `rvu->fwdata`—is completely absent from this function set, `has_bug` is false. Because there is also no added validation such as checking whether `rvu->fwdata` is present before use, this code does not itself show the fix either, so `is_fixed` is false.
